newsitem.title: UK: UK rate rise is BoE thumbs-down to budget - LibDems.
newsitem.headline: UK rate rise is BoE thumbs-down to budget - LibDems.

text.p: Thursday's rise in interest rates shows Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown failed in his budget last week to restore balance to the economy, Malcolm Bruce, economics spokesman for the Liberal Democrats, said.

"This is a big thumbs-down from the Bank of England to a budget which failed to tackle the imbalance in the economy between a robust consumer sector and a manufacturing sector which is being squeezed by the 25 percent appreciation of the pound," Bruce said in a statement.
He said the budget had failed because it put extra taxes on savers and firms instead of on an overheated consumer sector.
Bruce also blamed Brown's Conservative predecessor, Kenneth Clarke, for running a loose and irresponsible monetary policy in the run-up to the election.
"Never has a budget so welcomed on the day been so thoroughly discredited within the week. This was the week in which Labour's honeymoon ended," Bruce said.
Peter Lilley, economics spokesman for the main Conservative opposition party, also said the quarter-point rate rise to 6.75 percent was an inevitable consequence of the budget.

"In his budget, he diagnosed a consumer boom in order to justify him putting up taxes in contradiction to his election promises, but then he put the taxes not on consumer spending but on pension funds," Lilley told BBC radio.
